categories.main_business_segments: STUDIO ALICE operates two main business segments: the photo studio business, which includes children's photo studios and related services, and the costume manufacturing and wholesale business, which produces and supplies costumes for photo shoots and rental, primarily for children and coming-of-age ceremonies.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages professional studio photography techniques, digital image processing, and in-house production of photo prints. Costume manufacturing is handled both domestically (Kyoto) and in China, with a focus on quality control and cost efficiency. Automation and productivity improvements are emphasized in both photo production and costume manufacturing.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The primary customers are families with children, especially those celebrating milestones such as maternity, newborn, Shichi-Go-San (traditional Japanese children's festival), and coming-of-age ceremonies. The company also targets schools for school photo contracts and offers adult and baby photo services. Costume sales are mainly to internal group companies, with some external sales.
categories.geographic_coverage: Operations are concentrated in Japan, with over 400 photo studio locations nationwide, covering all major regions including Hokkaido, Tohoku, Kanto, Chubu, Kinki, Chugoku, Shikoku, and Kyushu. Overseas operations in Korea and Taiwan have been discontinued, and manufacturing is supported by a subsidiary in Shanghai, China.
categories.supply_chain_position: STUDIO ALICE is positioned downstream in the supply chain as a direct-to-consumer service provider through its photo studios. It is also vertically integrated upstream through its costume manufacturing subsidiaries, supplying both internal needs and some external customers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic focus is on selection and concentration within its core businesses, aiming to increase unit sales in maternity, baby, and Shichi-Go-San segments, and to expand the coming-of-age kimono rental and school photo businesses. There is an emphasis on operational efficiency, cost reduction, and adapting to changing customer needs. No significant R&D activities are reported.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated from studio photography services, including photo session fees and the sale of photo products. Additional revenue comes from costume rentals and sales, especially for coming-of-age ceremonies. Franchise fees and royalties are collected from franchisees, and licensing agreements (e.g., Disney character usage) also contribute.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: STUDIO ALICE is a leading player in the Japanese children's photo studio market, facing competition from other national and regional photo studio chains and independent studios. The company differentiates itself through scale, nationwide coverage, and exclusive licensing agreements (notably with Disney).
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending February 2025, consolidated sales were approximately 35.6 billion yen, with operating profit of 3.0 billion yen and net profit attributable to shareholders of 1.36 billion yen. The company has seen a slight decline in sales in recent years but improved profitability in the latest period. It maintains a strong equity ratio (over 70%) and a stable cash position.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: STUDIO ALICE emphasizes high-quality, memorable photography experiences for families, supported by a wide selection of costumes and exclusive character collaborations (notably Disney). Its nationwide network, in-house costume production, and focus on customer service and safety provide a unique value proposition in the Japanese market.
